learning: If s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m and steering_oscillation stays near 0.23 to 0.3, mass is no longer the limit at 0.4 kg; the next lever is geometry (wheel_track or sensor spread). If steering_oscillation rises while max_error does not move, the gains are the bottleneck for a light robot and the controller needs retuning.
notes: Iteration 5 controller and sensor layout unchanged; only mass changes from 0.5 to 0.4 kg (the allowed minimum). Tests whether further yaw-inertia reduction lowers s-bend max_error without raising oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg, score 422.9) is the best design so far. Against iteration 4 it raised the oval finish rate from 80% to 95%, cut oval steering_oscillation from 0.29 to 0.23, and lifted s-bend progress from 0.57 to 0.72, while the s-bend and slalom max_error (0.063 and 0.066 in iteration 4) stayed near the 0.06 m off-track limit. Mass has moved favourably at each step, and the lower steering_oscillation at 0.5 kg shows the existing gains are not overshooting. The Builder's proposal is a single-variable change, mass 0.5 to 0.4 kg (the allowed minimum), on the iteration 5 layout. I keep the controller identical to iteration 5 (kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction) so any change in results can be attributed to mass. Lower inertia means the same gains respond faster, so there is some risk of added oscillation; I am not changing gains pre-emptively because iteration 5 gave no sign of oscillation growth. The slalom line-loss problem (1.85 events) is a sensing-coverage issue, not a gain issue, so it is left for the Builder to address in a later geometry iteration. Expected result, not yet measured: s-bend max_error and progress improve, oval finish stays at or above 90%, and slalom is unchanged or slightly better.
